findings.paper_title: P&R 01 09 2026 Lease of part of Cattlemarket Car Park v2
findings.headline: Annual loss of £60,000 in car parking income will transfer to the new Unitary Authority's budget as an ongoing cost
findings.detail: Leasing 28 parking spaces for school use during school days and 6 permanently lost to layout changes reduces Cattlemarket Car Park income by approximately £60,000 annually. The County Council currently compensates Worcester for this loss until April 2028, but the Local Education Authority (new Unitary Authority after reorganisation) will bear the full cost thereafter, creating a structural budget impact for the successor authority.
findings.matters: Finance directors must account for permanent reductions in income. Lenders assessing councils' ongoing cash positions need to know about committed costs that directly affect future budget capacity and revenue available for debt servicing.
findings.figures: £60,000 per annum loss; 28 spaces under school use during school days; 6 spaces permanently lost; 216 total spaces in car park
findings.quote: It is estimated that the loss of car parking income, building in an increase in tariff, would be in the order of £60,000 pa. However, as the Local Education Authority, the new Unitary would have to bear this loss itself in the future.

findings.headline: Complaint resolution performance significantly below target at 79% versus 95% target
findings.detail: Only 79% of Stage I complaints were resolved at first contact in Q1 (30 of 38 complaints). This represents an 16 percentage point shortfall against the 95% target and suggests systemic service delivery issues.
findings.matters: High complaint escalation rates suggest operational and service quality problems that may indicate broader organisational challenges affecting financial management and delivery.
findings.figures: 79% resolved vs 95% target; 30 of 38 complaints
findings.quote: 79% (30 of 38) of all complaints received by the Council were resolved at Stage 1 of the complaints process.

findings.headline: Local government reorganisation reserve of £1.6m committed with major governance transition in October 2026
findings.detail: Worcester City has set aside £1.6m to cover its share of costs for the Transforming Worcestershire reorganisation into two new unitary councils, with transition to Voluntary Joint Committee(s) starting October 2026. This represents a major structural change with financial and operational risks.
findings.matters: Major local government reorganisation creates organizational disruption, transition costs, and uncertainty about future service delivery and financial management that affect lending risk.
findings.figures: £1.6m reserve
findings.quote: A reserve of £1.6m has been set aside to cover Worcester City's share of expected costs.

findings.headline: Medium Term Financial Plan delivery delayed by five months
findings.detail: The MTFP 2026-2031, which sets the council's financial direction, was originally due February 2027 but is now scheduled for July 2027. This was discussed at Group Leaders meeting in June 2026.
findings.matters: Delays in financial planning documents can indicate forecasting or analytical capacity issues and delay transparency on multi-year financial sustainability.
findings.figures: Original Due Date 28-Feb-2027; Current Due Date 28-Jul-2027
findings.quote: Discussed at Group Leaders meeting 1 June 2026 and reported to Policy and Resources Committee on 30 June 2026 - MTFP update report.

findings.headline: Scala and Corn Exchange project completion delayed by two years from original date
findings.detail: The major regeneration project has slipped from a planned March 2025 completion to June 2027. Main works continue but public realm delivery is now scheduled for early 2027, indicating material project delivery risk.
findings.matters: A 27-month delay on a capital project signals potential issues with project governance, cost management, and stakeholder delivery capability that lenders assess when evaluating council creditworthiness.
findings.figures: Original Due Date 31-Mar-2025; Current Due Date June 2027
findings.quote: The overall programme completion is now June 2027.

findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation creates structural uncertainty, with £1.6m earmarked for unitary authority transition costs
findings.detail: The council has created earmarked reserves specifically to support the costs of creating a new unitary authority, with £1.6m available for LGR and £0.330m for Community Governance Review. This signals the council is planning for structural change.
findings.matters: Major structural reorganisation creates uncertainty about the council's future borrowing capacity, governance continuity, and service transitions.
findings.figures: £1.6m allocated for LGR; £0.330m for CGR
findings.quote: Earmarked reserves have been created to support the costs of creating a new unitary authority as detailed in section 6

findings.headline: Earmarked reserves are planned to fall from £13.3m to £2.9m over two years, with business rates reserves depleting sharply
findings.detail: The council's earmarked reserves are forecast to fall by £10.416m between March 2026 and March 2028. Business rates reserves fall from £3.138m to £693m. Capital reserves (£1.959m) are expected to be fully deployed. This includes the £1.5m Scala Arts Centre drawdown noted above.
findings.matters: Rapidly depleting reserves reduce the council's capacity to manage contingencies and increases vulnerability to external shocks or forecast misses.
findings.figures: Earmarked reserves: £13.317m (March 2026) → £6.832m (March 2027) → £2.901m (March 2028); Business rates: £3.138m → £1.693m → £693m
findings.quote: Earmarked reserves are expected to reduce by £10.416m between March 2026 and March 2028

findings.headline: Crematorium closure for capital works creates income risk on bereavement services, with explicit project delay risk flagged
findings.detail: The Crematorium is closed for capital project to replace cremators. Bereavement Services income budget has been reduced by £700k to reflect the closure, with £655k currently forecast. The report explicitly flags risk: project delays could further compress this income.
findings.matters: Revenue-dependent services become risky when closed for capital works; project delays amplify revenue risk and reduce financial headroom.
findings.figures: £700k budget reduction; £655k currently forecast; project completion delays flagged as risk
findings.quote: there is risk on this due to delays on the completion date of the project

findings.headline: Planned savings of £1.073m are tracking to achieve only £1.003m, with £70k of initiatives delayed or facing reduced returns
findings.detail: Several savings initiatives are not yet achieved in Q1: Worcester Show sponsorship (£10k, described as 'ambitious'), Planning Performance Agreements (£15k), car parking provider renegotiation (£18k shortfall), black bin replacement charges (£17k, delayed by IT issues), and Diglis/Waterworks parking charges (£10k, still in consultation). These shortfalls are included in the Q1 forecast position.
findings.matters: Savings shortfalls reduce financial flexibility and suggest implementation risk on the council's deficit reduction strategy.
findings.figures: £70k of £1.073m (6.5%) not achieved; largest individual miss is car parking at £18k
findings.quote: The savings not yet achieved are detailed below and the adverse variances are included within the Q1 forecast outturn

findings.headline: Worcester City Council faces unbudgeted £1.5m pressure on the Scala Arts Centre capital programme
findings.detail: The report explicitly notes an unbudgeted pressure of £1.5m from the Scala Arts Centre capital project. This pressure has required drawdown from the council's contingency reserve and is noted as a separate agenda item for the committee.
findings.matters: Unbudgeted capital overruns indicate delivery risk on major projects and reduce the council's reserve buffer for other contingencies.
findings.figures: £1.5m unbudgeted pressure; used from contingency reserve
findings.quote: there is an unbudgeted pressure of £1.5m arising from the Scala Arts Centre capital programme

findings.headline: Scala Theatre and Corn Exchange regeneration projects are experiencing cost overruns requiring additional budget.
findings.detail: The Future High Streets Fund scheme (budget £4.943m, forecast £5.167m) and Cultural Investment Plan scheme (budget £3.706m, forecast £4.078m) are both overspending, combined overruns of £596k. Both projects are delayed to early 2027 completion instead of end of 2026. The report states a separate agenda item addresses a request for additional budget to cover these additional costs at the Scala Theatre and Corn Exchange.
findings.matters: Cost overruns on flagship cultural regeneration schemes signal delivery and project management risk. A council requesting additional budget mid-project on major public investments interests lenders assessing governance and financial discipline.
findings.figures: FHSF £224k over budget (£5.167m forecast v £4.943m budget); Cultural fund £372k over (£4.078m forecast v £3.706m budget)
findings.quote: Forecast spend for 2026/27 is £27.429m, and net pressure of £0.163m mainly relating to additional costs of the Public Arts Venue at the Scala Theatre and Corn Exchange

findings.headline: Council has £2.84m (15% of non-treasury investment portfolio) concentrated in loans to sports organisations with prior repayment reductions.
findings.detail: Non-treasury investments include: Worcester International Hockey £2.1m, Worcestershire FA £660k, Lower Wick Swimming Pool £76k (reduced from £98k originally), and Kiln CIC £4k (reduced from £20k originally). These are illiquid loans dependent on the viability of specific organisations. Two of the four loans have already undergone principal reductions, suggesting repayment difficulties.
findings.matters: These loans represent concentrated, illiquid exposure to third parties. Prior reductions on two loans (swimming pool, Kiln CIC) signal repayment stress. If any organisation fails, the council faces write-offs on top of already-depleting reserves.
findings.figures: Sports loans total: £2,839,933 of £18,975,233 total non-treasury investments (15%); Hockey £2.1m; FA £660k; Swimming Pool £76k (originally £97.8k); Kiln CIC £3.75k (originally £20k)
findings.quote: Loan to Worcester International Hockey = £2,100,000 ... Loan to Worcestershire F.A. = £660,101 (originally £750,000) ... Loan to Lower Wick Swimming Pool = £76,082 (originally £97,800) ... Loan to Kiln CIC = £3,750 (originally £20,000)

findings.headline: Strategic property fund investment shows £400k unrealised loss now masked by statutory accounting override expiring in April 2029.
findings.detail: The council holds a £3m investment in a CCLA Property Fund currently valued at £2.6m. The £400k loss exists but is deferred from the accounts under the statutory override for pooled investment funds. The paper states: 'The current value of the investment is £2.6m, fortunately due to the statutory override mentioned under paragraph 5.1 below this capital loss does not need to be realised within the Council's Income and Expenditure account.' This override expires 1 April 2029, at which point the loss must be absorbed.
findings.matters: This is a real £400k capital loss that will eventually require funding through reserves or budget cuts once the override expires. The deferral only masks the impact temporarily, and lenders assess real financial position rather than accounting treatments.
findings.figures: Investment principal: £3.0m; Current valuation: £2.6m; Unrealised loss: £0.4m; statutory override expires 1 April 2029
findings.quote: A principal amount of £3m is held in an externally managed strategic pooled Property Fund. The current value of the investment is £2.6m, fortunately due to the statutory override mentioned under paragraph 5.1 below this capital loss does not need to be realised within the Council's Income and Expenditure account.

findings.headline: Investment income collapsed 32% year-on-year from £1.1m to £741k, due to lower cash balances and falling rates.
findings.detail: Interest earned on short-term investments fell from £1,095,939 (2024/25) to £741,227 (2025/26), a drop of £354,712. The council's average investment balance also declined from £25.5m to £21.3m. Combined with falling interest rates (4.86% to 4.04%), this income pressure continues into 2026/27 as rates have fallen further.
findings.matters: Many councils budget for investment income to help balance operating budgets. A 32% drop in a year signals either deteriorating cash generation or reduced reserves available to invest, and when combined with lower rates, indicates sustained income pressure.
findings.figures: 2025/26 interest earned: £741,227; 2024/25: £1,095,939; decline £354,712 (32%); average investment balance fell from £25.5m to £21.3m
findings.quote: The Council achieved £741,227 of interest from its short-term investments in 2025/26 (2024/25: £1,095,939)

findings.headline: Council is holding £4.5m more external borrowing than the treasury liability benchmark deems necessary.
findings.detail: The council's optimal borrowing level (liability benchmark) is calculated at £13.1m for 2025/26, but actual external borrowing stands at £17.6m—an excess of £4.5m. This over-borrowing relative to capital spending needs suggests either deteriorating financial flexibility or that the council is borrowing to maintain liquidity for operational purposes beyond capital investment.
findings.matters: Over-borrowing relative to capital requirements may indicate the council is funding recurring budget pressures through debt rather than sustainable revenue. Lenders distinguish between borrowing for capital and borrowing to manage deficits.
findings.figures: Liability Benchmark: £13.1m; Actual External Borrowing: £17.6m; excess of £4.5m
findings.quote: Liability Benchmark 9.0 13.1 ... External Borrowing 14.9 17.6

findings.headline: Usable reserves fell by £6.3m (25%) in the year from £25.3m to £19.0m, forcing increased external borrowing.
findings.detail: The council's reserves contracted significantly during 2025/26. According to the report: 'Due to a fall in the balance of usable reserves there was a need to increase actual external borrowing to cover this increased CFR.' This £6.3m decline represents a material reduction in the council's financial buffer, and is not offset by capital spending—it reflects deteriorating underlying financial position.
findings.matters: Reserve depletion is unsustainable as a funding source and cannot be replenished from operations. Lenders care because it shows the council is drawing down its financial cushion rather than maintaining balanced budgets.
findings.figures: Usable reserves: £25.3m (31 Mar 2025) to £19.0m (31 Mar 2026); decline of £6.3m
findings.quote: Due to a fall in the balance of usable reserves there was a need to increase actual external borrowing to cover this increased CFR.

findings.headline: Supplier payment performance missed targets in both 30-day and 10-day metrics
findings.detail: Q4 2025-26 saw 92.5% of invoices paid within 30 days against a 100% target, and 87.4% of local supplier payments within 10 days against a 90% target. Both metrics missed, on consecutive quarters likely, suggesting sustained cash flow tightness or process degradation.
findings.matters: Payment performance deterioration can signal cash flow constraint or operational degradation; missed local supplier targets in particular may reflect working capital pressure.
findings.figures: 30-day target 100%, actual 92.5%; 10-day target 90%, actual 87.4%
findings.quote: For Q4 2025/26 performance was 92.5% paid on time.

findings.headline: Capital programme slippage of £5.744m (23%) with major delivery delays on Towns Fund and Future High Street
findings.detail: Against a budget of £25.171m, the council spent £19.426m with £5.744m carried forward. The two largest programmes—Towns Fund (£1.735m slippage) and Future High Street Fund (£1.486m)—account for over half the variance. About 20% of capital is financed by borrowing.
findings.matters: Material slippage suggests delivery risk on major regeneration schemes; the paper notes finance are working to improve forecasts, implying forecasting has been weak.
findings.figures: £5.744m slippage on £25.171m budget (23%); Towns Fund £1.735m; High Street £1.486m
findings.quote: Against the latest budget of £25.171m there was significant slippage of £5.744m in the programme

findings.headline: Bereavement Services income collapsed during crematorium refurbishment, with a £917k fees variance
findings.detail: The closure of Astwood crematoria during refurbishment had a cascading impact: a £209k adverse variance on the service itself after drawing down £819k from earmarked reserves, and an underlying £917k income variance on bereavement fees in Appendix 2. The paper notes the impact on 2026-27 was addressed in base budget, but the dependency on a single facility is evident.
findings.matters: Major income line (£1.6m annual budget) temporarily failed; this exposes the council to facility-dependent revenue risk and required reserve drawdown to mask the shortfall.
findings.figures: £917k fees variance (Appendix 2); £209k service adverse variance; £819k reserve applied
findings.quote: due to the cessation of alternative arrangements for cremations during the refurbishment of Astwood crematoria, there is an adverse variance of £209k

findings.headline: Business rates income shortfall will impact the 2027-28 budget with a £327k pressure
findings.detail: Lower actual business rates income created a £512k pressure in 2025-26 through reduced pool benefits. The council deliberately maintained its Business Rates reserve by not drawing down the budgeted £1.1m, explicitly noting that the shortfall will hit the 2027-28 accounts.
findings.matters: Forward-looking pressure on a major revenue stream that will constrain the 2027-28 budget; the council is flagging this as a known future deficit that must be managed.
findings.figures: £512k one-off pressure 2025-26; £327k forecast pressure 2027-28; £1.1m reserve held
findings.quote: The actual lower BR income will impact 27/28 budget so have maintained Bus Rates reserve by not drawing down budgeted £1.1m

findings.headline: External audit fees increased by £205k for additional work to build back reassurance
findings.detail: Worcester's audit costs rose significantly in 2025-26. The report specifically states this is for 'additional work to build back reassurance', though a £68k government grant partially offsets the impact. This language signals audit findings or control weaknesses that required remedial work.
findings.matters: Audit escalation and the need for 'reassurance' work suggests control deficiencies or prior audit concerns; this is a red flag for financial governance and internal controls.
findings.figures: £205k increase; £68k grant mitigation = £137k net impact
findings.quote: Audit costs –increased external audit fees estimation of £205k for additional work to build back reassurance. This is mitigated by MHCLG Local Audit Build-Back Grant of £68k.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Annual Report of Internal Audit
findings.headline: Council has not achieved full compliance with Local Government Transparency Code 2015: parking income surplus, fraud data, and individual purchase card items over £500 remain unpublished
findings.detail: Audit found that while most core Transparency Code requirements are met, full compliance has not been achieved. Specific data gaps: parking income surplus figures, fraud data, and individual corporate purchase card expenditure over £500. Management action is in progress to address these disclosure gaps.
findings.matters: Non-compliance with statutory transparency requirements undermines public accountability and may indicate gaps in the council's governance and disclosure processes
findings.figures: Three categories of data not published: parking income, fraud data, purchase card expenditure >£500
findings.quote: Whilst most core requirements are met, full compliance with the Transparency Code is not yet achieved. The audit highlighted that data had not been published for any parking income surplus, fraud data, and in relation to individual items of expenditure over £500 on corporate purchase cards.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Annual Report of Internal Audit
findings.headline: Corporate purchase card controls are incomplete: receipts not always returned, no value-for-money evidence required, some cardholders hold limits of £25,000, and expenditure over £500 is not published
findings.detail: Audit of 63 cardholders with total spend of £1,082,657 over 2020-2025 found receipts and transaction logs not consistently returned to Finance, creating VAT accounting and fraud prevention risks. There is no requirement for officers to evidence value for money, and high card limits exist. Corporate purchase card expenditure over £500+ is not published per Transparency Code. A new policy was agreed in June 2026 and cardholder list review is in progress.
findings.matters: Failure to return receipts increases VAT accuracy risk and fraud exposure; lack of value-for-money evidence and transparency weakens control over £1.08m in discretionary spend
findings.figures: £1,082,657 total spend 2020-2025; card limits range £500-£25,000; 63 cardholders
findings.quote: Receipts and transaction logs were not always being returned to the Finance Team as per the policy. This could result in an incorrect VAT return and is also a control to prevent fraud.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Annual Report of Internal Audit
findings.headline: Signed contract documentation cannot be located for some extended or amended contracts, and supplier payments have been made without corresponding contract register entries
findings.detail: Internal audit found examples where final signed contracts and documentation were missing, including for extended or amended contracts. Additionally, some payments to suppliers were not recorded on the contract register. A new contract register system is being implemented and scheduled for early 2026-27 to address this control gap.
findings.matters: Missing contract documentation and unregistered supplier payments indicate a control weakness that could allow unauthorized or unsupported payments to suppliers
findings.figures: Findings described as 'examples' but no aggregate value provided
findings.quote: The audit highlighted examples where final signed contract documentation could not be located. This included examples of extended or amended contracts. The audit also highlighted examples of payments to suppliers which were not recorded on the contract register.

findings.headline: External audit completion remains significantly behind the council's annual reporting cycle
findings.detail: The council identifies as an ongoing concern that external audit work is 'significantly behind the Council's annual reporting cycle'. This has persisted through 2025-26 and is flagged as a continuing governance priority for 2026-27.
findings.matters: Delays in audit completion delay closure of accounts and formal financial reporting. This creates governance risks and may constrain the council's ability to refinance, access capital markets, or demonstrate financial compliance to potential lenders.
findings.figures: Ongoing delay into 2026-27 reporting cycle
findings.quote: It continues to be of concern to the Council that the external audit work programme is now significantly behind the Council's annual reporting cycle.

findings.headline: Externally funded capital programmes facing escalating cost and staffing pressures
findings.detail: The council's capital programmes relying on external funding are described as 'challenging in terms of revenue and staffing' with 'cost pressures which are becoming more acute'. This represents a deteriorating position in capital delivery capacity.
findings.matters: Growing cost pressures may force the council to reduce scope, delay projects, or require additional internal funding to deliver externally-funded schemes. This could impact the council's ability to deliver its city regeneration agenda and economic development priorities.
findings.figures: Externally funded capital programmes including Scala Arts Centre, Angel Place regeneration, and Shrub Hill zone
findings.quote: The Council's externally funded capital programmes were challenging in terms of revenue and staffing as well as cost pressures which are becoming more acute.

findings.headline: Council required to sell assets to support delivery of priorities and balance budget
findings.detail: The council's financial future is explicitly described as 'very challenging'. While the government funding settlement provided some stability, the council identified asset sales as a necessary income source alongside other sources to balance the budget and fund service delivery.
findings.matters: Reliance on asset sales to balance budgets signals structural revenue shortfalls that cannot be covered by normal funding sources. While one-off in nature, it suggests the council is drawing down capital assets to meet revenue commitments.
findings.figures: Sale of assets identified as required income source
findings.quote: The Council's financial future continues to be very challenging. The revised funding settlement from Government has provided some stability but the Council has had to identify other sources of income (including sale of assets) to support the delivery of its priorities.

findings.headline: Auditors have issued a disclaimed opinion on the 2025-26 accounts
findings.detail: Azets provided a disclaimed auditors opinion on the accounts rather than a clean opinion, due to the national backlog of local authority audits and backstop arrangements. The auditors have proposed a 3-year plan to build back assurance on the accounts.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion is the weakest form of audit opinion and means the auditor cannot give reasonable assurance over the financial statements. This would concern any lender evaluating the reliability of the council's financial position and reporting.
findings.figures: 31 March 2026 accounts, 3-year assurance rebuild plan
findings.quote: In February 2026 Audit and Governance committee received Completion Reports for the year's ended 31 March 2026 from Azets, but these accounts have a disclaimed Auditors opinion. Azets have provided Audit and Governance Committee with a plan to build back assurance over a 3 year period.

findings.paper_title: Feb Council MTFP and Council Tax
findings.headline: Financial sustainability designated as high-risk (rating 9) on the Corporate Risk Register
findings.detail: The council formally identifies 'Financial Sustainability' as a key corporate risk: inability to deliver the MTFP due to reduced government funding, difficult macroeconomic conditions, insufficient resources, increased costs and demand. The risk is rated 9, indicating it is treated as material by the council's governance framework.
findings.matters: The council has formally flagged financial sustainability as a material strategic risk, validating the plan's acknowledged vulnerabilities. The identified risk drivers—funding uncertainty, pay inflation, business rates volatility, council tax collection, and capital scheme delivery—align with issues flagged in the plan itself.
findings.figures: Risk rating 9; risks include capital delivery, EPR funding, pay inflation, business rates, council tax collection, council reorganisation (£400k budget), VAT partial exemption
findings.quote: The Council is unable to deliver the Medium-Term Financial Plan (MTFP) due to reduced local government funding, difficult macroeconomic conditions, insufficient resources, increased costs and demand for services. The current risk rating is 9

findings.paper_title: Feb Council MTFP and Council Tax
findings.headline: Statutory food waste collection duty (£870k estimated annual cost) has no confirmed ongoing funding
findings.detail: The government mandated weekly food waste collection from all households by March 2026 and provided one-off capital grants totalling £1.196m. However, the council estimates £870k of annual ongoing revenue cost from this service, and central government has not confirmed ongoing funding—only that it 'will be distributed via the new proposed new funding formula'.
findings.matters: This is a statutory obligation with a known, material cost (£870k per year) that has no confirmed funding source. If the new funding formula does not deliver, the council must meet this cost from its own budget, creating a structural deficit risk.
findings.figures: £870k estimated annual revenue cost; £299k revenue grant + £897k capital grant received; implementation target April 2027
findings.quote: an ongoing revenue budget to support this new burden has not been confirmed, only that funding will be distributed via the new proposed new funding formula

findings.paper_title: Feb Council MTFP and Council Tax
findings.headline: £700k one-off cost pressure in 2026-27 from Astwood Crematoria closure and stalled restart
findings.detail: The council has closed Astwood Crematoria for refurbishment and used contingency funds during 2025-26 when alternative arrangements were suspended. The facility will not restart until Q3 2026-27, creating a £700k one-off revenue pressure as a revenue-generating service remains offline for an extended period.
findings.matters: This one-off cost stress-tests the budget and represents material loss of revenue from a commercial-style operation. It also signals capital project delivery risks—the refurbishment was planned to complete mid-September 2026 but service won't restart until Q3.
findings.figures: £700k one-off pressure in 2026-27; capital works completion target mid-September 2026; service restart Q3 2026-27
findings.quote: By not restoring services until quarter 3 of 2026-27, there will be a one-off pressure in the region of £0.700m which has been built into the 2026-27 expenditure forecasts within the MTFP

findings.paper_title: Feb Council MTFP and Council Tax
findings.headline: Earmarked reserves to fall 43% over three years, with grants reserve collapsing from £4.55m to £724k
findings.detail: Table 4 shows total earmarked reserves declining from £11.49m (31 Mar 2025) to £6.55m (31 Mar 2027)—a 43% reduction. The Grants reserve, typically held for flexibility and contingencies, falls from £4.553m to £724k. The CFO's statement that 'if there are opportunities to replenish reserves, these should be taken' indicates concern about the depletion rate.
findings.matters: Rapid reserve depletion leaves the council with less buffer for unexpected costs or income shortfalls. The Grants reserve is traditionally the most flexible contingency tool; its collapse to £724k is a material loss of financial flexibility.
findings.figures: Total earmarked reserves: £11,490k (31.3.25) → £6,549k (31.3.27); Grants reserve: £4,553k → £724k; General Fund balance £1.4m (9% of net expenditure)
findings.quote: if there are opportunities to replenish reserves, these should be taken

findings.paper_title: Feb Council MTFP and Council Tax
findings.headline: Business Rates deficit of £1.9m in 2025-26, driven primarily by check, challenge and appeal outcomes
findings.detail: The 2025-26 business rates forecast shows a £1.9m shortfall, primarily due to the outcome of ratepayer appeals through the check, challenge and appeal (CCA) process. This £1.9m variance—versus the budget set in 2025—demonstrates how volatile business rates income can be and how much the council is exposed to appeals by individual ratepayers.
findings.matters: Business rates volatility from appeals creates uncontrollable income swings. A £1.9m impact in one year represents 12% of general government grant and shows the council's income is vulnerable to ratepayer actions outside its control.
findings.figures: £1.9m deficit in 2025-26 forecast mainly from check, challenge and appeal process
findings.quote: the forecast position for 2025-26 is a deficit of £1.9m mainly relating to the outcome of a check, challenge and appeal process

findings.paper_title: Feb Council MTFP and Council Tax
findings.headline: Budget balance depends on £1.78m of non-guaranteed Extended Producer Responsibility funding
findings.detail: The plan states explicitly that all years are balanced but heavily reliant on Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) funding. For 2026-27, £1.78m is budgeted, but this is not guaranteed—it will only materialise if PackUk recovers sufficient funds from producers to fund it. Any shortfall would immediately create a budget gap.
findings.matters: About 12% of the planned spending increase depends on funding the council cannot control or guarantee. This creates a material downside risk to the plan's deliverability and would require emergency savings or reserves drawdown if EPR income falls short.
findings.figures: £1,781,633 anticipated for 2026-27; 'additional funding (up to the £1.741m) is not guaranteed'
findings.quote: However, an ongoing revenue budget to support this new burden has not been confirmed, only that funding will be distributed via the new proposed new funding formula.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Worcester City Council Audit Completion Report- 31 March 2025
findings.headline: No material adjustments to reported financial outturn identified from completed audit work; no significant value-for-money weaknesses
findings.detail: Where audit work was completed, the auditor identified no material misstatements affecting the reported outturn — only minor disclosure and classification amendments, all agreed by management. Value-for-money testing identified no significant weaknesses in the Council's arrangements for securing economy, efficiency and effectiveness. Quality indicators across all completed areas — statement timeliness, working paper quality, finance team accessibility, error volumes — are marked green.
findings.matters: These findings provide assurance that, where completed, audit work found no fundamental errors and that the Council's accounting processes and financial management are sound. This suggests the disclaimer is procedural (inability to complete work within time) rather than reflecting underlying financial mismanagement or concealed problems.
findings.figures: No material audit adjustments; no significant VFM weaknesses; all quality indicators green
findings.quote: From the work we have completed we have not identified any adjustments to the financial statements which impact the Council's reported financial outturn for 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Worcester City Council Audit Completion Report- 31 March 2025
findings.headline: Auditor cannot formally verify going concern assumption despite no identified material uncertainties
findings.detail: The auditor has not obtained sufficient audit evidence to formally conclude on going concern, though they have not identified any material uncertainties about the Council's ability to continue as a going concern. This procedural gap arises from inability to complete the full audit before the statutory backstop date. Management prepared the accounts assuming continuation of services with no intention to transfer services outside the public sector.
findings.matters: Going concern is fundamental: financial statements prepared on any other basis would indicate insolvency or restructuring. Inability to obtain auditor verification means a lender cannot rely on formal audit confirmation of the Council's continuing viability in its current structure.
findings.figures: Backstop date: 27 February 2026
findings.quote: As we have been unable to conclude our audit in advance of the backstop date, we have not been able to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to enable us to conclude that a material uncertainty related to going concern has not been identified

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Worcester City Council Audit Completion Report- 31 March 2025
findings.headline: Reserve movements and closing balances not fully verified; accuracy of year-on-year movements unable to be concluded
findings.detail: The auditor analysed reserve movements across all disclaimed years (2021/22–2024/25) and reconciled them to financial statements for internal consistency. However, they explicitly state the accuracy of reserve movements cannot be concluded because 'the movements and the closing balance are directly influenced by the opening balance' — which is unverified due to prior disclaimers. This work will continue into 2025/26. Reserves represent the Council's available financial cushion.
findings.matters: Reserve balances determine a council's financial flexibility to absorb budget pressures, unexpected costs, or changes in income. Unverified reserve positions mean uncertainty over actual available resources and the reliability of any reserve strategy or buffering disclosed to the market.
findings.figures: Reserve analysis covers four years: 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24, 2024/25
findings.quote: Not been able to conclude the accuracy of the movements as the movements and the closing balance are directly influenced by the opening balance.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Worcester City Council Audit Completion Report- 31 March 2025
findings.headline: Pension liability valuation and movements remain unaudited due to prior year disclaimers and time constraints
findings.detail: The Council's net pension asset of £2,907k could not be audited. Work was limited by lack of assurance over opening balances from prior disclaimed years — the auditor has no assurance on year-on-year pension movements, interest costs, investment returns or asset contributions since 2020/21. The triennial actuarial valuation is scheduled for 2025/26, so detailed work is deferred. The auditor cannot verify the accuracy of the 2024/25 pension valuation or challenge actuarial assumptions.
findings.matters: Pension liabilities are highly sensitive to actuarial assumptions (discount rates, inflation, mortality rates, pay growth) and represent long-term obligations. An unaudited pension position means uncertainty over whether the Council faces unexpected funding calls or is over-provisioning, affecting financial flexibility and potential future contribution rate changes.
findings.figures: Pension assets and liabilities (net): (£2,907)k; triennial valuation due 2025/26
findings.quote: We have not been able to gain any assurance over year-on-year movements, interest costs, interest on assets, actual return on asset, share of assets and service costs due to the prior year balances being disclaimed, meaning we have no assurance over opening balances.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Worcester City Council Audit Completion Report- 31 March 2025
findings.headline: Property, plant and equipment (£105.2m) and investment property (£16.1m) valuations were not audited in 2024/25
findings.detail: The auditor performed no audit procedures on valuations of land and buildings or investment property. The Council plans a full asset portfolio revaluation in 2025/26, so all valuation audit work was deferred to that year. These highly material valuations involving complex judgement and estimation would normally require detailed audit testing on fair value, market evidence, depreciated replacement cost assumptions, and impairment indicators. PPE additions, disposals and depreciation were tested with no issues found.
findings.matters: Combined property assets of £121.3m form a material part of the Council's balance sheet and are usually the largest asset category in local authority accounts. Without audit verification of valuations, a lender cannot confirm asset backing, market value, or whether investments in property are appropriately valued or impaired.
findings.figures: Property, plant and equipment: £105,214k; Investment properties: £16,135k; combined total £121,349k
findings.quote: The Council intend to revalue its asset portfolio in 2025/26, as a result, no audit procedures were performed in relation to the valuation of land and buildings in 2024/25 and we are unable to reach a conclusion in this area.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Worcester City Council Audit Completion Report- 31 March 2025
findings.headline: Auditor will disclaim opinion on 2024/25 financial statements, following disclaimed opinions for three consecutive prior years
findings.detail: The auditor intends to issue a disclaimed opinion on the Council's 2024/25 accounts, unable to express a view on whether the financial statements give a true and fair view. This follows disclaimed audit opinions for 2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24. The disclaimer is driven by inability to regain assurance over opening balances from prior years and to complete audit work on property valuations and pension liabilities before the 27 February 2026 statutory backstop date, despite substantially completing all planned work.
findings.matters: A disclaimed audit opinion removes all auditor verification from reported financial balances. For a lender, this creates fundamental uncertainty about the Council's true financial position, asset backing, and ability to service borrowing. For the finance director, it signals a break in audit continuity and unresolved issues in financial reporting.
findings.figures: Four consecutive years with disclaimed or unmodified-unable opinions (2021/22 through 2024/25); backstop date 27 February 2026
findings.quote: Due to the challenges of undertaking an audit where the previous three years have been disclaimed, it has not been possible for us to undertake sufficient work to regain full assurance and support an unmodified audit opinion ahead of the backstop date of 27 February 2026.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Worcester City Council Draft 24-25 Audit Opinion
findings.headline: The audit certificate cannot be formally concluded pending completion of Whole of Government Accounts work.
findings.detail: The auditors cannot issue the final audit certificate for 2024-25 until the Whole of Government Accounts work is completed and certified by the National Audit Office. While they state this does not have a material effect on the statements or value-for-money conclusion, the certificate remains delayed.
findings.matters: A delayed or uncompleted audit certificate indicates the audit process is not fully concluded, which affects the formal sign-off of the Council's accounts.
findings.figures: Year ended 31 March 2025
findings.quote: We cannot formally conclude the audit and issue an audit certificate for Worcester City Council for the year ended 31 March 2025 in accordance with the requirements of the Local Audit and Accountability Act 2014 and the Code of Audit Practice (the "Code") until we have completed all our responsibilities mandated by the Code.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Worcester City Council Draft 24-25 Audit Opinion
findings.headline: The audit was defective in its ability to detect fraud or irregularities.
findings.detail: Because the auditors could not obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence, they were unable to reliably detect irregularities or fraud that may exist within the Council's financial statements.
findings.matters: A defective fraud detection capability represents a control failure and governance weakness that directly affects financial risk assessment.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: The audit was defective in its ability to detect irregularities, including fraud, on the basis that we were unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Worcester City Council Draft 24-25 Audit Opinion
findings.headline: Opening balances and prior-year comparatives cannot be verified due to cascading disclaimed opinions in previous years.
findings.detail: The auditors were unable to obtain evidence over the 2023-24 comparative figures because of previously disclaimed opinions. As a result, they could not determine whether adjustments were needed to opening balances as at 1 April 2024, with consequential effects on the year-end 2024-25 figures.
findings.matters: If opening balances are not verified, the reported position for 2024-25 is built on an unconfirmed foundation, making it impossible to track year-on-year financial movement with confidence.
findings.figures: Opening balances as at 1 April 2024; year ended 31 March 2025
findings.quote: we were unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence over the disclosed comparative figures for the year ended 31 March 2024 by the backstop date as a result of disclaimed opinions in previous financial years. Therefore, we were unable to determine whether any adjustments were necessary to the opening balances as at 1 April 2024

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Worcester City Council Draft 24-25 Audit Opinion
findings.headline: Auditors have issued a disclaimer of opinion on the Council's financial statements for 2024-25.
findings.detail: The auditors were unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence by the backstop date (27 February 2026) to form an opinion on whether the financial statements are free from material misstatement. They state that undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive, affecting net assets, usable and unusable reserves, and income and expenditure figures.
findings.matters: A disclaimer of opinion means the Council's reported financial position cannot be relied upon, which is critical for any lending decision and for the finance director's understanding of the council's true position.
findings.figures: 27 February 2026 (backstop date)
findings.quote: We have concluded that the possible effects on the financial statements of undetected misstatements arising from these matters could be both material and pervasive. We have therefore issued a disclaimer of opinion on the financial statements.
